text: In 1669, a man boiled urine to make gold. Hennig Brand, in Hamburg, hoped to find gold hiding inside it. He boiled down vats of it for days. No gold. Instead, a white paste that glowed in the dark. He'd found phosphorus, the first element with a known discoverer.
